title: POC: GDPR-focused prompt retention & workload sizing
summary: Kickoff scoping for a limited POC focused on GDPR-sensitive prompt handling. Discussed success metrics (latency, throughput, PII redaction accuracy), workload sizing (qps, tokens per request), benchmark plan, retention matrix and timeline for pilot. Agreed next steps: share security artifacts, run a short benchmark with redaction enabled, and align on success criteria and rollback policy.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Mark Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (CortexBank Head of Data Privacy), Samir Patel (Platform), Tina Lo (ML)

Summary (auto): short POC scoping, gdpr constraints, ephemeral prompt storage preference, benchmark sizing notes.

[00:00] Mark: thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you making time, my name is Mark Chen, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Elena: hey thanks, quick note we have a hard requirement that all eu customer PII is handled under gdpr controls and retention cannot exceed 30 days for prompts containing ssns or bank ids unless encrypted and expressly permitted, so want to get that on the table.
[00:22] Priya: totally understood. for the poc we usually propose two tracks: ephemeral prompts (no storage) and controlled storage with KMS and retention policy. want to scope which you prefer for the first run.
[00:35] Samir: ideally ephemeral to start, but we need a way to repro issues and audit—so maybe ephemeral by default with optional hashed prompt logs and full plaintext only for support with customer consent.
[00:48] Tina: also we need to validate redaction quality. our internal SLO is 99% redaction for phone numbers / ssns on recall tests. is that something Redwood can surface?
[01:02] Priya: we can run a benchmark with our redaction pipeline + custom regex layer; we also support model-side prompt-scrubbing and prefix filtering. we should define a test corpus to measure precision/recall, that will be part of the benchmark.
[01:18] Elena: okay good. timeline wise, compliance wants the initial report within two weeks so we can sign off for the pilot.
[01:25] Mark: two weeks is tight but feasible for a small benchmark. action items and owners we'll capture.

---
[05:10] Priya: workload sizing: to size Dedicated or estimate hosted cost, we need qps, average tokens per request, percent of streaming sessions, and expected concurrency. can you share current peak qps?
[05:20] Samir: peak for the feature is about 35 qps, average 12 qps during business hours. typical payload is a 300 token prompt, expected generation 150 tokens. 40% of calls will be streaming, concurrency spikes to about 55 simultaneous sessions.
[05:40] Priya: great that's helpful. with those numbers we recommend running a benchmark at 1.5x peak to validate autoscale and P95 latency under load. so target test qps = 52 qps, sustained for 10 minutes, with bursts to 80 qps for 2 minutes.
[06:02] Mark: for cost estimates we can provide per-token and per-minute perf numbers; we'll include a few configuration profiles: hosted standard, hosted with aggressive batching, and dedicated small pool.

[09:00] Tina: about prompt storage — we have two concerns: 1) ability to mark certain flows ephemeral so no prompt is written to disk, and 2) a retention matrix where high-risk prompts are retained 0 days, medium-risk 7 days, low-risk up to 30 days. can your retention policies be per-route or per-model?
[09:22] Priya: yes per-route retention is supported at the config layer. we also support tags on requests (e.g., risk=high) so the policy engine can drop or encrypt accordingly. retention enforcement is done at the control plane and audit logs show retention actions—these logs can be retained separately per your compliance needs.
[09:44] Elena: audit log retention itself is sensitive, we want minimal retention of extracted metadata but need an immutable audit trail for access -- 1 year for audit, but access logs must be pseudonymized. can you support pseudonymization via hashing with customer-managed KMS?
[09:58] Priya: yes we support holding KMS keys in customer cloud (bring-your-own-kms) for encryption at rest and we can hash identifiers before writing logs—there's an option for reversible encryption for forensic pulls with an approval workflow.

[12:30] Samir: latency SLOs: our product requires p50 < 120ms and p95 < 450ms for single-turn gen with 150 tokens output. can Redwood meet that on a hosted tier?
[12:45] Priya: depends on model choice and batching. on our standard medium-latency models we've seen p50 ~ 80ms for small models and p95 around 300-400ms at your load, but streaming has different characteristics. for guaranteed p95 targets we recommend dedicated pool or lower-batch thresholds. we'll propose a configuration that meets those SLOs in the report.

[15:00] Elena: security checklist — SOC2, ISO 27001, data processing agreement, data residency (eu region), SSO/SAML for console, audit log export. can you send the compliance pack?
[15:12] Mark: we'll attach our SOC2 report, dataproc addendum, and a short doc on VPC/private connector options.
[15:20] Elena: also want to confirm no human-in-the-loop access to raw prompts unless explicit support case with a ticket.
[15:29] Priya: default is automated. we have an internal support workflow which requires customer approval to access decrypted payloads and everything is logged.

---
[19:00] Tina: for the benchmark dataset, we will provide a 10k example corpus with 20% containing synthetic ssns and PHI to validate redaction and for latency we'll include 1k of heavy-context examples with long KV caches. is 10k enough?
[19:18] Priya: that's a good start. for statistical significance on redaction recall/precision we'd prefer 25k but 10k with a focused 2k sensitive subset will give us actionable results in two weeks.
[19:30] Samir: do you need us to anonymize the corpus or can you accept encrypted blobs?
[19:36] Priya: encrypted blobs are fine; if you provide keys we can run tests in a private deploy, or you can provide synthetic but realistic examples. either works.

[22:00] Mark: success criteria — let's document a candidate set now: 1) redaction recall >= 99% on SSN/phone tests; 2) p95 latency <= 450ms under 1.5x peak qps; 3) no persistence of high-risk prompts (0 day retention); 4) audit trail + pseudonymized logs accessible to CortexBank; 5) runbook for data subject requests within 72 hours. agree?
[22:26] Elena: those look good; add also a criteria that any decrypt-for-support must be request+approval within console and visible in audit logs.
[22:35] Mark: noted. we'll add that as item 6.

[25:00] Priya: benchmark plan: week 0 share artifacts and dataset; week 1 run functional redaction tests and a short load test; week 2 run extended soak at 1.5x and produce final report. do you expect a hardware-based private run?
[25:20] Samir: we'd prefer hosted for speed but may require a dedicated private run if encryption keys cannot be shared. we'll try hosted with BYOK first.
[25:33] Tina: can you run the redaction tests both with model-side scrubbers and our regex pre-filter to compare?
[25:40] Priya: yes we'll run A/B within the benchmark and include metrics for false positives and false negatives and gold labels.

[29:10] Elena: about retention enforcement, how does your system guarantee deletion? is it a tombstone or actual wipe? we need certifiable deletion for high-risk flows.
[29:22] Priya: deletion is a multi-step: control-plane policy marks objects for deletion, we run a secure wipe on the storage shard and remove from backups based on retention cycle. for high-risk flows we can enforce immediate deletion and produce a deletion certificate for the object id.
[29:42] Samir: backups—how long before snapshots might rehydrate deleted prompts?
[29:48] Priya: backups live in encrypted snapshots; retention policy for backups is configurable per account. for PII we recommend no snapshots containing plaintext PII; if you must retain, snapshots should only contain encrypted blobs under your BYOK and separate retention.

[33:00] Mark: pricing for the POC? we'll provide a short proposal but typical POC is credits for hosted usage plus engineering time. for dedicated temp pool we can do a short-term reserved for the two-week run.
[33:18] Samir: send the pricing and also a tiny estimate for a dedicated 'troubleshoot' node we can spin up if we hit perf issues.

[36:00] Tina: edge case: what if model hallucination exposes sanitized data — e.g., model reconstructs masked tokens? can redaction cause the model to still leak via paraphrase?
[36:16] Priya: good catch. we will include an adversarial test where we probe for reconstructability. there's a mitigation: we can run out-of-model output filters and apply post-generation redaction. also recommend truncating or tokenizing PII before model. we'll include paraphrase tests in the benchmark.

[39:40] Elena: accountability: we need a contact for data subject requests, and a commitment to respond within 72 hours. who will be the Redwood contact?
[39:50] Mark: primary contact will be me for commercial and Priya for technical escalation; we'll provide a dedicated CSM if pilot expands.

[41:00] Priya: technical notes to include in the report: request-level tags, per-route retention policy, BYOK KMS flow, hashed audit export, deletion certificate generation, redaction benchmarking methodology, and A/B metrics.

[43:10] Mark: recap of agreed next steps and owners.
[43:15] Elena: quick clarification — can we hide certain tokens from telemetry entirely? we need no derivative logs for high-risk flows.
[43:24] Priya: yes, you can opt route to suppressed telemetry; that will remove the ability to trace request contents in hosted analytics but we'll provide meta-level metrics.

[45:00] Mark: ok wrap up: thanks all, we'll send the benchmark plan and security pack today, schedule the benchmark for next Tuesday, and follow up on action items.
[45:12] Elena: thanks, looking forward to the report.
[45:18] Samir: thanks everyone.

End of transcript
action_items: Priya Rao | Prepare benchmark plan and A/B redaction matrix | 2027-05-07
Mark Chen | Send SOC2 report, DPA, and BYOK integration docs | 2027-05-05
Samir Patel | Provide workload telemetry and 10k corpus (encrypted) | 2027-05-06
Tina Lo | Supply gold-label sensitive subset of 2k examples and regex filters | 2027-05-06
next_steps: Share compliance pack (SOC2/ISO/DPA) via secure link
Schedule hosted benchmark for 2027-05-11 at 09:00 UTC
Deliver POC pricing + short dedicated node estimate by 2027-05-05
